definition: Cacophony means a harsh, jarring mixture of loud, discordant sounds.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word cacophony. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know cacophony should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: When the parrots, the barking puppies, and the squeaky exercise wheels all started up at once, the pet store filled with a cacophony that sent customers hurrying back out the door.
Noise is any unwanted sound, even a single humming fan; a cacophony is a whole tangle of loud, clashing sounds hitting the ear at once.
Pandemonium goes beyond cacophony, adding wild, uncontrolled chaos and confusion on top of the deafening sound.

A din is a loud, unpleasant noise that goes on and on, like the din of highway traffic. Its defining feature is sheer relentless volume. A cacophony is defined instead by clash: many sounds fighting one another, harsh and discordant even when none of them is very loud.

Clamor is the loud outcry of many people, a crowd of voices shouting at once, often demanding something. A cacophony need not involve voices or demands at all: it is any harsh, grating mix of clashing, discordant sounds, human or not.

A racket is a loud, disturbing noise, like the neighbors' racket at midnight. Like a din, a racket is measured in volume and annoyance. A cacophony is measured in discord, in how badly the sounds clash, which is why even a quiet cacophony grates on the ear.

The orchestra's new symphony filled the hall for nearly an hour, and the audience sat spellbound to the final note.
Cacophony means a harsh, jarring mixture of loud, discordant sounds.

Five minutes before rehearsal, the middle school band room erupted: trumpets blatted scales, drummers pounded on rims, and a clarinet shrieked its highest note, a cacophony that made the director cover her ears.
Every instrument is producing its own loud sound at the same time, with nothing blending or harmonizing.
That jumbled, grating wall of clashing noise is exactly what cacophony names.

Cacophony most often appears in the pattern 'a cacophony of' followed by the sound sources, as in 'a cacophony of horns' or 'a cacophony of voices.' Do not confuse it with symphony, which shares the 'sound' root but names organized, harmonious sound; a cacophony is the opposite, sound with no order or blend at all.

The food festival had booked three bands to play on three small stages, one at each end of the square and one in the middle.
Each group sounded fine on its own, and none of them played very loudly.
But near the fountain, where all three drifted together, brass collided with banjo and a drum machine argued with a waltz, and the mixture curdled into cacophony.
Visitors winced and drifted toward the edges of the square, where a single stage dominated and the music untangled itself.
The organizers later admitted the problem was never volume; it was that the sounds fought one another wherever they met.
